variations.name: Plant-based meat (ground, whole-cut, 3D-printed)
variations.description: Replicates ground, formed, or whole-cut meat from plant proteins (soy, pea, wheat) using extrusion, shear-cell, or 3D-printing to mimic muscle texture, cutting the land, water, and emissions footprint of livestock by roughly an order of magnitude.
variations.white_space: The ground/burger segment is mature but in retail decline in the US/EU as the early flexitarian wave fades; the credible opening is premium whole-cut (steak, bacon, chicken filet) at sub-conventional price and clean labels, where texture and ingredient-deck simplicity, not novelty, win shelf space.

companies.name: Beyond Meat
companies.what: Publicly traded maker of pea/rice/fava-protein burgers, sausages, and jerky sold across US retail and global foodservice.
companies.signal: 2025 revenue guidance ~$320-335M, down double digits YoY; closed up to $100M senior secured debt facility from Ahimsa-affiliated Unprocessed Foods to shore up balance sheet

companies.name: Impossible Foods
companies.what: Plant-based beef, sausage and chicken differentiated by soy-leghemoglobin (fermentation-derived heme) for a meaty taste; consolidated heme IP after settling its suit with Motif.
companies.signal: Private; one of the two largest US plant-meat brands; acquired Motif's HEMAMI heme IP via 2024 litigation settlement

companies.name: Redefine Meat
companies.what: Israeli firm 3D-printing plant-based whole cuts (flank steak, lamb) as 'New-Meat' for European restaurants and retail.
companies.signal: Launched next-gen flank steak across Europe; won a 5-star Great Taste Award 2025

companies.name: Juicy Marbles
companies.what: Slovenian maker of plant-based whole-cut filet mignon, loins and ribs sold through European grocery.
companies.signal: ~$4.6M raised; in ~3,500 stores (Tesco, Sainsbury, Waitrose, Whole Foods, Lidl); planned 2025 US retail launch and targeted profitability by year end

companies.name: Steakholder Foods
companies.what: Nasdaq-listed (STKH) developer of 3D bioprinting hardware (MX200, HD144 printers) for printed meat and seafood structures, sold as B2B equipment/IP.
companies.signal: Began revenue generation in 2024 via a sales agreement with Bondor Foods; opened first full-scale demonstration center

companies.name: Tattooed Chef
companies.what: Former SPAC-listed plant-based frozen-meals brand that failed to differentiate in a crowded category.
companies.signal: Filed Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2023 and sold assets after running out of cash

companies.name: Hooray Foods / Nowadays
companies.what: San Francisco startups making plant-based bacon (Hooray) and plant-based nuggets (Nowadays) for retail/foodservice.
companies.signal: Both ceased production and wound down in 2024; Hooray cited 'economics... do not match our revenue'

variations.name: Plant-based dairy, cheese & yogurt
variations.description: Recreates milk, cheese, and yogurt from plant bases (oat, soy, nut, potato) plus plant proteins/fats and cultures, avoiding the methane and land use of dairy herds while targeting the harder functional challenge of meltable, stretchy cheese.
variations.white_space: Plant milks are mature, but plant cheese still trails dairy on melt/stretch/flavor and shelf economics; the opening is a plant casein-mimic (e.g. Bettani's Caseed) that delivers true mozzarella performance without precision fermentation's bioreactor cost.

companies.name: Oatly
companies.what: Publicly traded Swedish oat-milk pioneer that built the barista/coffee plant-milk category worldwide.
companies.signal: Largest pure-play plant-milk brand globally; public (Nasdaq: OTLY)

companies.name: Bettani Farms (formerly Climax Foods)
companies.what: US cheese-alternative producer using a data-driven plant casein-mimic ('Caseed') to target stretchy mozzarella; rolling up the category.
companies.signal: Rebranded from Climax with $6.5M Series A and a new CEO (ex-Califia CFO); acquired Hungry Planet, Numu and Stockeld Dreamery

companies.name: Miyoko's Creamery
companies.what: US cultured plant-based cheese and butter brand using traditional fermentation of cashew/legume bases.
companies.signal: Established premium plant-cheese brand in US natural and conventional grocery

companies.name: Nobell Foods
companies.what: Makes casein in genetically engineered soybeans (plant molecular farming) to deliver real melting/stretching cheese functionality.
companies.signal: ~$103M raised from Y Combinator, a16z and Breakthrough Energy Ventures

companies.name: Stockeld Dreamery
companies.what: Swedish fermented plant-based cheese maker (cultured cream cheese, slices) built on a legume base.
companies.signal: Raised $20M Series A; shut down in 2024 amid plant-based decline, with a last-minute asset acquisition by Bettani Farms keeping its cream cheese on shelf

variations.name: Plant-based eggs & seafood
variations.description: Replaces eggs (mung-bean or other plant-protein liquid eggs) and fish/shellfish (konjac, soy, legume, algae) with plant analogues, easing pressure on caged hens and on overfished and bycatch-heavy wild stocks.
variations.white_space: Plant seafood is the weakest segment: low repeat purchase, thin margins, and a string of closures/asset sales (New Wave). The opening is whole-muscle, nutritionally fortified analogues (omega-3, B12) for high-value species rather than crumb/surimi formats that compete on price.

companies.name: Eat Just (JUST Egg)
companies.what: Maker of mung-bean-based liquid and folded plant eggs; the dominant US plant-egg brand, now also extending to a 'Just Meat' plant-chicken line.
companies.signal: Former unicorn (>$1B valuation); secured new funding in 2025; launched three plant-chicken flavors

companies.name: Konscious Foods
companies.what: Vancouver maker of frozen plant-based sushi, onigiri and poke (a world-first frozen vegan-sushi line) for retail and foodservice.
companies.signal: $26M seed round; founded 2021 by Gardein/Yves founder Yves Potvin

companies.name: Bayou Best Foods
companies.what: Plant-based seafood (shrimp) venture launched by Big Idea Ventures using IP acquired from the defunct New Wave Foods.
companies.signal: Newly launched on acquired alt-shrimp IP; early stage

companies.name: New Wave Foods
companies.what: Pioneer of plant-based shrimp from algae and plant proteins for foodservice.
companies.signal: >$20M raised since 2015; wound down with its IP sold to Big Idea Ventures' Bayou Best Foods

companies.name: Gardein (Conagra)
companies.what: Conagra-owned mainstream plant-protein brand with plant-based fish filets and crab cakes alongside meat analogues.
companies.signal: Owned by Conagra Brands; broad US retail distribution

variations.name: Mycoprotein & filamentous-fungi / biomass fermentation
variations.description: Grows whole filamentous fungal biomass in fermenters (the cells themselves are the food), yielding a fibrous, high-protein, high-fiber ingredient that is the most cost-mature fermentation route to meat-like texture and is economically viable at industrial scale today.

companies.name: Quorn (Marlow Foods / Monde Nissin)
companies.what: Original mycoprotein brand (Fusarium venenatum), launched 1985; now also supplies its mycoprotein as a B2B ingredient.
companies.signal: Owned by Monde Nissin; longest-running, widely deployed mycoprotein platform with broad regulatory approval

companies.name: ENOUGH (ABUNDA)
companies.what: Scottish firm producing ABUNDA mycoprotein via submerged fermentation as a B2B ingredient from its Sas van Gent (Netherlands) plant.
companies.signal: Raised ~$43.6M; doubling Netherlands capacity from 10,000 to 20,000 tonnes with a second line online in early 2025

companies.name: Nature's Fynd
companies.what: US producer of Fy fungal protein (Fusarium strain from Yellowstone) for dairy-free yogurt, meatless patties and bites.
companies.signal: >$500M equity+debt raised; backers include Gates, Bezos and Generation IM

companies.name: Infinite Roots
companies.what: German mycelium-fermentation platform converting biomass into food ingredients; partners with CPG firms for market entry.
companies.signal: €58M (~$85.7M) Series B in 2024 (Europe's largest mycelium round); partnership with Pulmuone in South Korea

companies.name: Planetary
companies.what: Swiss firm producing mycoprotein as a B2B ingredient and licensing its BioBlocks biomass-fermentation platform to turn agricultural side-streams into protein.
companies.signal: ~$28M raised (CHF 16M Series A + credit); exploring India production with Dhampur Bio Organics targeting sub-$1/kg

companies.name: Meati Foods
companies.what: US maker of whole-cut mycelium 'steaks' and cutlets (MushroomRoot) from its large Thornton, Colorado plant.
companies.signal: Raised ~$450M historically but hit a severe 2025 cash crisis: lender seized cash reserves, ~150 layoffs, plant closure, and assets sold for ~$4M

companies.name: Mycorena
companies.what: Swedish maker of Promyc fungi-based protein with meat-like texture for the food industry.
companies.signal: Filed for bankruptcy in July 2024 after scale-up and funding pressures

variations.name: Precision fermentation of dairy proteins (whey, casein)
variations.description: Engineers microbes (yeast/fungi) to brew the exact whey and casein proteins found in cow's milk without any animal, enabling animal-identical cheese, milk and protein powders with a fraction of dairy's emissions once production scales.
variations.white_space: Bioreactor capacity and unit cost remain the binding constraints; several leaders have paused or pivoted to contract manufacturing rather than build their own mega-plants. The opening is asset-light protein supply through CDMOs plus regulatory-cleared GRAS ingredients sold B2B to legacy dairy brands.

companies.name: Perfect Day
companies.what: Pioneer of fermentation-derived whey protein (beta-lactoglobulin) sold as a B2B ingredient to consumer brands worldwide.
companies.signal: Market leader with >32% share of precision-fermented dairy in 2024; >$825M raised; new Gujarat (India) plant on track for H2 2026 start and 2027 ramp

companies.name: Remilk
companies.what: Israeli maker of fermentation-derived whey protein, commercialized in 'New Milk' (a low-sugar, lactose-free dairy line) with Gad Dairies.
companies.signal: ~$150M raised; paused its planned Denmark mega-plant and pivoted to a European contract manufacturer; launched barista milk in coffee shops late 2025

companies.name: Imagindairy
companies.what: Israeli producer of animal-free whey protein targeting price parity, working with Strauss Group on cow-free drinks and cream cheese.
companies.signal: ~$30M+ raised; received FDA 'no questions' GRAS letter; secured access to 100,000 L of fermentation capacity with room to triple

companies.name: Formo
companies.what: German firm making microbial casein and koji-protein cheeses; among the first to bring fermentation-enabled cheese to European retail.
companies.signal: Among top-5 precision-fermented dairy players; received €35M (~$40.6M) backing from the European Investment Bank

companies.name: Vivici
companies.what: Dutch spin-out (dsm-firmenich/Fonterra heritage) selling nature-identical fermentation-derived whey protein and now lactoferrin as B2B ingredients.
companies.signal: €32.5M Series A; self-affirmed GRAS and US launch of whey in year one; launched fermentation-derived lactoferrin; exploring a 4M-L Abu Dhabi facility with The EVERY Company

companies.name: New Culture
companies.what: San Francisco firm using precision fermentation to make animal-free casein for cow-less mozzarella aimed at pizzerias.
companies.signal: Raised $25M Series A; partnered with CJ CheilJedang on scale-up

companies.name: Standing Ovation
companies.what: French firm producing casein via precision fermentation, preparing a US launch.
companies.signal: Raised ~€25M ($28.5M) Series B plus ~€5M non-dilutive funding

variations.name: Precision fermentation of egg, heme & specialty proteins (collagen, etc.)
variations.description: Brews specific functional proteins beyond dairy, egg white (ovalbumin), heme/myoglobin for meat flavor, and collagen for food and cosmetics, by fermenting engineered microbes, delivering animal-identical functionality without hens, cattle, or slaughterhouses.
variations.white_space: Heme has effectively consolidated into one player (Impossible) after Motif's collapse, leaving little competition; the opening is regulatory-cleared, GRAS-affirmed egg-white and specialty proteins sold B2B into bakery, sports nutrition and cosmetics where animal supply is volatile.

companies.name: The EVERY Company (formerly Clara Foods)
companies.what: Pioneer of precision-fermented egg-white proteins (ovalbumin, soluble egg protein), commercialized in beverages and protein powders.
companies.signal: Two ingredients commercialized in the US; launched FERMY protein powders with Landish; exploring a 4M-L Abu Dhabi facility; received US DoD biomanufacturing grant

companies.name: Onego Bio
companies.what: Finnish/US firm making animal-free egg protein (Bioalbumen, ovalbumin) via fungal precision fermentation for the US market.
companies.signal: $40M Series A plus €14M EIC Accelerator funding; on track for self-affirmed GRAS / FDA no-objections on Bioalbumen

companies.name: Geltor
companies.what: US firm producing designer bioengineered collagen and other proteins via precision fermentation, primarily for cosmetics/personal care and nutrition.
companies.signal: Market leader cited for animal-free collagen with strong brand recognition; commercial ingredient sales

companies.name: Impossible Foods (heme)
companies.what: Produces soy-leghemoglobin (heme) via precision fermentation to give plant meat its meaty taste; now also holds Motif's HEMAMI myoglobin IP.
companies.signal: Heme is core to its products; consolidated competing heme IP via the 2024 Motif settlement

companies.name: Shiru
companies.what: US firm using AI-guided discovery plus fermentation to produce novel functional proteins (e.g. emulsifiers, structurants) for food applications.
companies.signal: Cited among precision-fermentation ingredient players with an AI-led protein-discovery platform

companies.name: Motif FoodWorks
companies.what: Ginkgo spin-out that made HEMAMI heme/myoglobin and other functional ingredients for plant meat via precision fermentation.
companies.signal: Wound down in September 2024 days after settling Impossible Foods' IP suit; sold its heme business to Impossible

variations.name: Animal-free fats & oils (fermented or synthetic)
variations.description: Produces fats and oils, dairy-style butterfat, meat fat, and palm-oil replacements, either by fermenting microbes (precision/biomass) or by building triglycerides thermochemically from captured carbon, addressing the fat fraction that drives much of the flavor, melt and deforestation impact of animal and palm products.
variations.white_space: Fats are a high-value, under-served leverage point: a 1% animal-fat inclusion can transform plant-meat flavor, so B2B 'designer fat' suppliers win without needing to own the finished product. The constraint is fermentation cost; carbon-to-fat thermochemistry (Savor) is a novel, capacity-light alternative still proving cost at scale.

companies.name: Nourish Ingredients
companies.what: Australian firm making precision-fermented animal-like fats (e.g. Tastilux) that mimic meat/dairy fat at low inclusion rates, sold B2B.
companies.signal: Cleared to sell animal-free meat fat in the US (FEMA GRAS); set up a European commercial hub in the Netherlands; courted by global food giants

companies.name: Savor
companies.what: Bill Gates-backed firm building fats thermochemically from captured CO2, hydrogen and methane, no animals, plants or microbes; launched a carbon-made butter.
companies.signal: Launched first commercial product (carbon butter) in March 2025; planning a large-scale facility to take on dairy and palm

companies.name: C16 Biosciences
companies.what: US firm fermenting a palm-oil alternative (Palmless / Torula-derived oil) to replace deforestation-linked palm in food and personal care.
companies.signal: Achieved commercial-scale production with revenue in personal care; received US DoD biomanufacturing award; expanding into food

companies.name: Melt&Marble
companies.what: Swedish precision-fermentation firm making designer fats/lipids for food and personal care.
companies.signal: Closed ~$8.5M (SEK 80M) round in Dec 2025; reached commercial-scale production; first ingredients (personal care) in 2026, US food market in sight

companies.name: NoPalm Ingredients
companies.what: Dutch firm fermenting yeast on agri-food side-streams to produce a sustainable palm/coconut-oil alternative.
companies.signal: Cited among the active fermentation-fat players scaling a palm replacement

companies.name: Yali Bio
companies.what: California firm using synthetic biology and precision fermentation to design tailored fats and lipids.
companies.signal: Early-stage; cited among US precision-fermentation fat developers

variations.name: B2B plant-protein ingredients, isolates & texturization tech
variations.description: Supplies the upstream building blocks, pea/soy/wheat protein concentrates and isolates plus textured vegetable proteins made by high-moisture extrusion, that downstream brands turn into meat and dairy analogues; this layer is the most cost-mature and profitable part of the value chain.
variations.white_space: This is a crowded, incumbent-dominated commodity layer; differentiation is shifting to clean-label, neutral-tasting isolates and high-moisture textured proteins with chicken-like fiber, where formulation know-how rather than raw tonnage creates pricing power.

companies.name: Roquette
companies.what: Global leader in pea (and now wheat) protein under the NUTRALYS brand, including new large-chunk textured pea and textured wheat proteins.
companies.signal: Launched NUTRALYS T PEA 700XC (70% protein) and first-ever textured wheat protein T WHEAT 600L in 2025

companies.name: ADM
companies.what: Agribusiness giant supplying soy and pea protein concentrates, isolates and textured proteins, plus flavor/formulation services to plant-based brands.
companies.signal: One of the largest global plant-protein ingredient suppliers; integrated crop-to-ingredient operations

companies.name: Ingredion
companies.what: Ingredient maker offering pea and other plant protein isolates/concentrates and starches for protein fortification and meat/dairy analogues.
companies.signal: Broad commercial plant-protein portfolio (pea isolates, starches) sold B2B globally

companies.name: Cargill
companies.what: Agribusiness major supplying soy and pea proteins, textured proteins and fats/binders into the alt-protein supply chain.
companies.signal: Global plant-protein and texturant supplier with integrated sourcing

companies.name: PURIS
companies.what: US vertically integrated pea-protein producer (seed-to-isolate) that has been a key North American pea-protein supplier (notably to Beyond Meat).
companies.signal: Largest North American pea-protein producer; Cargill-backed expansion

variations.name: Fermentation scale-up infrastructure & contract manufacturing (CDMOs)
variations.description: Builds and operates the large fermentation tanks and downstream processing that protein startups lack, providing commercial-scale (100,000 L+) capacity as a contract manufacturer; this is the single biggest bottleneck standing between precision-fermentation pilots and price-competitive supply.
variations.white_space: Dedicated food-grade large-scale fermentation capacity is acutely scarce, only a handful of players have committed to 100,000 L+ food plants, so capital intensity and offtake risk keep entrants few. The opening is purpose-built food CDMOs (vs. repurposed pharma capacity) financed by sovereign and strategic capital with anchor offtake contracts.

companies.name: Liberation Bioindustries (formerly Liberation Labs)
companies.what: Purpose-built precision-fermentation CDMO; constructing a 600,000-L food-grade plant in Richmond, Indiana with dedicated downstream processing to supply startups like Vivici.
companies.signal: Raised ~$50.5M (plus $31.5M strategic from NEOM); Indiana plant slated to begin operations in early 2026; planned global network scaling to millions of liters

companies.name: Synonym
companies.what: US firm providing financing, engineering and project development to build out fermentation biomanufacturing capacity and match startups to capacity.
companies.signal: Cited as a key infrastructure/enablement player bridging startups to commercial fermentation capacity

companies.name: Cauldron
companies.what: Australian firm commercializing a continuous (hyper-fermentation) process and planning a network of 'smaller, smarter' precision-fermentation plants run as a CDMO.
companies.signal: Planning a 500,000-L facility; long-term CDMO network ambitions for functional lipids, enzymes and proteins

companies.name: ScaleUp Bio
companies.what: Singapore-based precision-fermentation CDMO (Temasek/ADM-linked) offering pilot-to-commercial capacity for food-protein startups in Asia.
companies.signal: Cited as an interim CDMO path for startups bridging lab validation to commercial supply

companies.name: ABEC
companies.what: Engineering firm designing and building large bioreactors and single-use/stainless fermentation systems used by food and biotech producers.
companies.signal: Established bioprocess-equipment supplier enabling large-scale fermentation buildouts
